content:
Apple has filed a lawsuit against OpenAI alleging theft of trade secrets, and the case has now been reassigned to U.S. District Judge Edward Davila, replacing the magistrate judge originally assigned to handle it. Details of the case are as follows.

Following the reassignment, the hearing originally scheduled for October has been cancelled.

When a civil lawsuit is filed in the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of California, it is randomly assigned to a district judge or magistrate judge. If the case is assigned to a magistrate judge, all parties must indicate whether they consent to that judge presiding over the case with full authority.

This is because district judges have the authority to preside over federal civil cases from start to finish, whereas magistrate judges may only do so with the consent of all parties.

On the same day Apple filed suit against two former employees, OpenAI, and Jony Ive's io Products for alleged theft of trade secrets, the case was randomly assigned to Magistrate Judge Virginia K. DeMarchi.

This means all parties in the lawsuit had to submit a form indicating whether they consented to Judge DeMarchi presiding over the case with full authority.

Apple appears to have refused this arrangement. The company yesterday filed a "consent or declination" form (which has not yet been made public), and this form appears to have triggered the process of reassigning the case to a district judge.

Since no other documents explaining the reassignment could be accessed, there is strong speculation that Apple chose to decline having a magistrate judge preside over the case.

The case has therefore been reassigned to U.S. District Judge Edward Davila, with Magistrate Judge Nathanael Cousins handling discovery-related matters.

Following the reassignment, the initial case management conference originally scheduled for October 13 before Judge DeMarchi has been cancelled and must be rescheduled before Judge Davila.

However, two other sets of deadlines remain in effect: parties must meet and confer on a settlement proposal and discovery plan by September 22, then submit initial disclosures and a joint case management statement by October 6.
